decisions.statement: A sample is taken every five seconds from the kernel's own counters.
The processor reading is the share busy between one sample and the sample before.
The first sample answers no processor reading, since a share needs a sample before it.
The memory reading is read whole off one sample.
The processor share is kept as a whole percent.
The memory reading is kept in the gigabytes its own readout answers.
A sample finding the reading the sample before found writes nothing.
A reading is kept beside the readout that reading was taken for.
A sample finding no reading keeps what the readout already holds.
Every twelfth sample writes the moment beside the sampler's own service page.
That moment is where the sampler leaves for code that moved.
A sample that throws ends the run rather than being caught and logged.
Where every page named here sits is asked of the index rather than spelled.
Nothing here starts a child process.
Nothing here carries a reading to a site.
Nothing here turns a share into a color.

definition: the workstation's processor and memory readings, taken on a beat and kept beside their readouts
